messages.subject: Problems of analysis of dung densities
messages.subject_clean: Problems of analysis of dung densities
messages.body_plain:
Dear Fellow distance maillisters,
Let me begin by intorducing myself. My name is Amirtharaj Christy
Williams and I am doing my Ph.D. on elephants in a National Park in
north India. As a part of my work I have been doing transects to
estimate elephant dung densities in a very hilly terrain. Therefore, it
has not been always possible to lay a perfectly straight line transect.
Sometimes we do rock climbing on steep slopes (slight exagerration
should be forgiven) when we are doing the transects. Because dung piles
are immovable object the question of recounting does not arise. We also
have exact distance to the dung piles from the center of the line to
each dung pile. The questions I have are;

1. Will densities calculated from such transects be valid?

2. Has any simulation study been done comparing curvilinear with
straight line transects?

3. I have problem in running the Distance dos version in batch mode on
transect replicates which do not have any dung piles. The error message
I get is 'unexpected end of data encountered" and the program exits.

I would be much obliged to hear your feedbacks on this.

regards and thanks for your valuable time,
A. Christy Williams

messages.body_plain:
> > 1. Will densities calculated from such transects be valid?

Possibly, provided they are representative on the ground in general.  If
you systematically avoid steep slopes, and the elephants do too, you will
overestimate numbers.

> > 2. Has any simulation study been done comparing curvilinear with
> > straight line transects?

I don't know - but curved lines are perfectly OK if they're random ...
your problem is that both you and the elephants may find the flatter
terrain easier, so you may oversample areas preferentially used by the
elephants.

> > 3. I have problem in running the Distance dos version in batch mode on
> > transect replicates which do not have any dung piles. The error message
> > I get is 'unexpected end of data encountered" and the program exits.

I suggest you switch to the windows version - available free from the www
site below.  The Dos version works fine though ... you're probably missing
a ';':

sample/label='line 1'/effort=1.2;
 ;
sample ...

is the format needed ... note the ';' on the second line.

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: (Fwd) Re: Models with no adjustments
messages.body_plain:
Your analysis sounds OK.  I would suggest doing some comparative
analyses with a larger truncation distance, just to check that the results
are consistent.  The issues of size bias are all familiar - especially
with those of us who have spent too much time in International Whaling
Commn meetings.  In fact, the regression methods in DISTANCE handle these
sources of bias quite adequately, provided estimates of size are OK close
to zero.  The slope can sometimes go the 'wrong' way, due to
underestimation of size of distant groups.  If this is suspected, then
keep the correction.  (In fact, I wonder whether we should change DISTANCE
so that we don't discourage people from using the regression when the
slope has the wrong sign ...)  The problem of cluster definition affects
the shape of the detection function, but provided a regression method of
correcting size bias is used (preferably the default method), this doesn't
cause bias.  It DOES cause bias of course if you just estimate mean size
by the mean size of recorded groups - we need a good estimate of mean size
AT ZERO DISTANCE.

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: JOB: University of St Andrews
messages.body_plain:
UNIVERSITY  OF  ST ANDREWS

           School of Mathematical & Computational Sciences

                    Research Assistant/Fellow

Two 1-year posts for applied statisticians exist in the Research Unit for
Wildlife Population Assessment (RUWPA). With the right applicants, job-share
arrangements for either post would be possible. The appointees will be
involved in one or more of the following projects: development of generalised
additive model (GAM) methods for estimating fish biomass; development of
methods for assessing fish discard rates; spatial modelling of wildlife
populations from line transect surveys; development of methods for improving
survey based estimation of fish abundance using GAMs and/or state-space models
and/or Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.

You should have a good honours degree in statistics, or in biology, maths or
applied maths with a strong statistical background. Experience with one or
more of the following would be an advantage: line transect sampling or
fisheries assessment methodology; S-Plus; generalised linear models; GAMs;
MCMC methods.

Salary will be at the appropriate point on the 1A or 1B scale for research
staff, i.e.د15,735- د23,651 per annum. Informal enquiries may be made to Dr.
David Borchers (tel. +44 (0) 1334 463806, e-mail d...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk) or
Prof. Stephen Buckland (tel. +44 (0) 1334 463787, e-mail
st...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk). More information on RUWPA can be found at
http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/.

Please quote ref: KC117/AMC1/99		Closing Date: 29 April /99

Application forms and further particulars from Personnel Services, University
of St Andrews, College Gate, North Street, St Andrews, Fife KY16 9AJ, (tel:
01334 462571, by fax 01334 462570 or by e-mail Job...@st-andrews.ac.uk). We
regret applications cannot be made by e-mail.
